# nuclis

> A local inference engine for open-weight models on Apple Silicon, written from scratch in Zig with a Metal backend and built around Qwen3.8-27B, with Gemma 4 E4B as its small model and a small coding agent (`nuclis agent`) and typed decision models (`nuclis decide`, `nuclis serve`) on top. Every model runs first on nuclis's own CPU reference, and the Metal kernels are checked against it. MIT licensed; experimental, version 0.x.

- Runs on macOS on Apple Silicon, with Metal; releases also ship an x86-64 Linux build that runs on the CPU only. Download a release binary or build with Zig 0.17.1.
- Models are pinned to a repository, commit and SHA-256, with one default per kind: Qwen3.8 27B for chat (with a DFlash2 drafter), Laya for decisions, EmbeddingGemma 2, Qwen3-TTS 1.7B CustomVoice, and Nemotron ASR. The verified extras are Gemma 4 E4B QAT and Inkling 2 Mini for chat, clef-flash for decisions, and VoiceTut-TTS for Egyptian Arabic speech; `nuclis model pull --catalogue` fetches the defaults and `--extra` adds these. Archived entries (Gemma 4 12B and 26B-A4B, Muse Glimmer 30B, Drama 3, the other Qwen3-TTS checkpoints) still pull and run by name.
- Speech in and out: Qwen3-TTS 1.7B CustomVoice speaks, Nemotron 3.5 ASR streaming 0.6B transcribes live or whole recordings, Gemma 4 E4B hears clips; served as OpenAI's `/v1/audio/speech` and `/v1/audio/transcriptions` and a WebSocket for live transcription.
- Speculative decoding is on by default where it measured faster.
